subject: Finishes that help a workspace feel calm
hook: That thin line around your shelves is louder than you think
ig:
That thin line around your shelves is louder than you think.

On a home office wall, every edge is a line your eye has to process. A contrasting edge, such as a white edge on a grey shelf or a dark line on an oak-effect door, outlines each panel. Multiply that by twelve shelves and six doors and the wall starts to feel busy, even when it's empty.

Colour-matched ABS edging does the opposite. The edge takes the same colour as the face, so each panel reads as one simple block.

When contrast does work: one deliberate feature, like a desk top in oak-effect against charcoal cupboards. Used once, it's a design choice. Used everywhere, it's noise.

Which would you choose for your desk wall: matched edges everywhere, or one contrast feature? Tell us in the comments.
fb:
A small detail we always raise when planning a home office: the colour of the edges.

When the edging contrasts with the door or shelf, every panel gets an outline, and a whole wall of storage can start to feel busy. Matching the ABS edge to the face lets each piece read as a single block of colour, which is far easier to sit in front of all day. If you want some contrast, we'd suggest using it once, say an oak-effect desk top against charcoal cupboards, rather than everywhere.
